title: Learning Interestingness in Automated Mathematical Theory Formation

publication.venue: The Thirty-ninth Annual Conference on Neural Information Processing Systems

mechanism.domainTask: Learning programmatic interestingness measures for automated mathematical theory formation in FERMAT
mechanism.populationDetail: EvoAbstract maintains four island populations of interestingness programs; each generation samples one island uniformly, evolves there, and periodically runs abstraction extraction across all islands.
mechanism.archiveDetail: No separate elite archive is described; high-scoring programs are sampled from island populations for evolution and abstraction, while abstraction libraries store reusable subroutines rather than elite candidates.
mechanism.replacementDetail: Algorithm 1 updates the sampled island as \(P_i\) <- \(P_i\) union {\(P\)}; no survivor pruning or separate elite archive update is specified.
mechanism.generationDetail: Lvar performs LLM-driven evolution using sampled high-performing parent programs as source material and synthesizes candidate interestingness programs through complex mutations; the prompt requests a new function rather than a localized edit.
mechanism.feedbackDetail: Fitness is cumulative extrinsic reward across FERMAT episodic rollouts; scores are used to identify high-performing parent programs and samples for abstraction extraction.
mechanism.parentSelectionDetail: Parents are sampled among high-performing programs within the uniformly sampled island; \(n_p\) is not numerically specified in the reported settings. The abstraction library supplies references but is not an additional parent pool.
mechanism.outOfTaxonomy: Periodic LLM-based abstraction extraction builds per-island reusable subroutine libraries that modify the future program search space; this auxiliary learned library is neither an elite candidate archive nor a separate generation operator.
